subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Which non-zero exec outcomes should suppress user-visible channel failure warnings without hiding genuine command failures?
rationale: The existing `completed` status describes process lifecycle rather than command success, so source inspection cannot infer whether maintainers want explicit accepted-exit metadata, unconditional non-zero warnings, or broadly quiet normal exits.

options.title: Add an accepted-exit signal
options.body: Preserve non-zero failure warnings by default and suppress them only when the exec or observer path explicitly marks the outcome as accepted or handled.

options.title: Quiet all normal exits
options.body: Treat every `status: "completed"` result as non-error and intentionally accept that genuine normally exited command failures may no longer warn.

options.title: Keep current warning semantics
options.body: Retain non-zero classification and require commands with expected non-zero outcomes to express that intent, such as through their command construction.

recommendation.title: Add an accepted-exit signal
recommendation.body: Preserve non-zero failure warnings by default and suppress them only when the exec or observer path explicitly marks the outcome as accepted or handled.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work introduced the shared orphan-tool-error warning behavior whose intended semantics must be preserved or deliberately changed.
